My biggest issue is the absolutely terrible level 1 setup that's strictly worse than the Ranger's and the Paladin's. Rangers get favored enemy AND favored terrain. Paladins get Divine Sense AND Lay on Hands AND Heavy Armor.

Right off the bat, Rangers get more options. Your character feels more...you. You're choosing how he develops, which counters his weak start (compared to other classes, like Barbarian).

Paladins get more combat bonuses at low levels and their Divine Sense could be used to find the same enemies, even if they fly or are invisible.

Level 2 also works out better for the two default classes.

Rangers get spellcasting, with solid spells to deal massive damage early on. Dual wield while using Hunter's Mark for an additional 2d6 damage every turn, and can chain from target to target. Hail of Thorns on a bonus action to deal 1d10 (average 5.5) on everything within a 3x3 square, on top of your basic damage, and it's only halved on a save (so about 2 damage).

Paladins get access to Dueling, which provides roughly the same damage (2) as the Witch Hunter's Blood Rite (the average of a 1d4 is 2.5) but with no life or bonus action lost. Paladins are still better.

I like the idea of a witch hunter, but it should have been made as a prestige class. Maybe with the requirements being a ranger with Mage Slayer and either Undead, Fey, Celestial, or Fiend as a favored enemy. Ranged attacks get added to Mage Slayer, with a 15 foot range instead of 5. And maybe has "Witch Hunter spells", but they can only be cast with a sacrifice ability, consuming max HP equal to double the spell slot level, and gaining regen equal to the spell slot level, and being able to strike as a bonus action after casting. I can see something like that working out.

I guess I'm disappointed by the Witch Hunter's early game, with nothing more interesting than "I hit you very hard" being an option. Everything until level 6 just adds damage with little decision making. The only thing I can think of that's nearly as boring is the Champion Fighter.
